justification.STREET/BUILDINGNUM: street and house-number parts of the postal address -> ADDRESS (the dataset has no whole-address label)

label_source: README: 20-class Open PII labelset; the 20 labels were confirmed from the validation file for the five kept languages (label counts only).

out_of_scope_reasons.CITY/ZIPCODE: coarse geography alone (policy: public places in general are not masked); masking them as part of a full address region is neither rewarded nor penalised
out_of_scope_reasons.DATE: generic calendar date; the dataset has no date-of-birth label so birth dates cannot be separated (policy: generic dates are do-not-mask)
out_of_scope_reasons.TITLE/SEX/GENDER: salutation/title and demographic attributes without a policy label

policy_note: Policy labels and their definitions come from configs/privacy-policy-v1.json. A source label is in scope only when it clearly is one of the 16 policy labels; everything else is out of scope (neither recall nor excess; the share that still got masked is reported). All annotated spans (in and out of scope) count as annotated for excess.
sample: language in {en,de,fr,it,es}; per language sha256(source_text utf-8) ascending, first 1000 rows (5000 total); gold = privacy_mask start/end/label
